note: Main lessons for every book of the Bible, Genesis to Revelation. Fields: b=book id, t=theme, kv=key verse, ls=main lessons, c=where the book points to Christ.

books.t: Beginnings: creation, fall, and the promise
ls: God created everything good, and humanity in His own image.
Sin entered through one act of distrust and broke everything — but God pursued the sinners, not abandoned them.
God builds His plan through covenant promises to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and preserves His people through Joseph.
books.c: The offspring who will crush the serpent (3:15), the lamb God Himself provides (22:8), and Judah's coming ruler (49:10) all point to Jesus.

books.t: Redemption: God delivers and dwells
ls: God hears the cry of the oppressed and acts in mighty power to free them.
Salvation comes through the blood of the Passover lamb, not the merit of the rescued.
God gives His law and His presence — the redeemed are made a worshiping people.
books.c: Jesus is our Passover Lamb (1 Cor 5:7), the true bread from heaven, and the greater Moses who leads the ultimate exodus from sin.

books.t: Holiness: a holy God makes a way to be near
ls: Sin is costly — atonement always requires a substitute's blood.
God is holy, and His people are called to be distinct in every area of life.
The Day of Atonement shows both the seriousness of sin and the mercy of God.
books.c: Every sacrifice, priest, and cleansing ritual is a shadow fulfilled in Jesus, our great High Priest and final sacrifice (Hebrews 9-10).

books.t: Wilderness: faithfulness meets unbelief
ls: Unbelief, not obstacles, keeps people out of God's promises.
God provides daily — manna, water, guidance — even for grumblers.
God keeps His promises across generations despite human failure.
books.c: The bronze serpent lifted up for the dying is Jesus' own picture of His cross (John 3:14-15).

books.t: Covenant renewed: love the LORD your God
ls: Obedience flows from remembering what God has done.
God's commands are for our good — life and blessing are found in loving Him.
Choose this day: covenant faithfulness is a decision every generation must make.
books.c: Moses promises a greater Prophet to come (18:15) — fulfilled in Jesus, who kept the whole covenant we broke.

books.t: Conquest: God keeps every promise
ls: Courage comes from God's presence, not favorable odds.
Victory belongs to the LORD — Jericho fell to faith, not siegecraft.
Not one word of God's good promises ever fails.
books.c: Joshua ('The LORD saves') leads Israel into rest — a preview of Jesus (same name in Greek), who leads His people into eternal rest.

books.t: The spiral of sin and the mercy of God
ls: When everyone does what is right in their own eyes, society collapses.
God repeatedly raises deliverers for an undeserving people.
Flawed judges cannot produce lasting peace — the heart itself must change.
books.c: Every failed deliverer sharpens the longing for the perfect Deliverer-King, Jesus.

books.t: Loyal love in the darkest times
ls: God works His grand plan through small, ordinary faithfulness.
Hesed — costly loyal love — is the family likeness of God's people.
The outsider who takes refuge under God's wings is fully welcomed in.
books.c: Boaz the kinsman-redeemer buys back a foreign widow — and their line leads straight to David and to Jesus, our Redeemer (Matt 1:5).

books.t: The heart God sees: kingship begins
ls: God exalts the humble (Hannah) and brings down the proud (Eli's house).
Man looks at outward appearance; the LORD looks at the heart.
Obedience is better than sacrifice — partial obedience is disobedience.
books.c: David the anointed shepherd-king from Bethlehem prefigures great David's greater Son.

books.t: David's throne and God's forever promise
ls: God's covenant with David promises a throne established forever.
Even the man after God's own heart falls terribly — and repentance, not perfection, marks the godly.
Sin is forgiven yet consequences remain; grace is never license.
books.c: The son of David whose kingdom never ends is Jesus (Luke 1:32-33).

books.t: A kingdom divided by half-hearted worship
ls: Wisdom without wholehearted devotion ends in idolatry (Solomon).
How long will you go limping between two opinions? God demands undivided loyalty.
God is not in the noise but often in the low whisper — He sustains His weary servants.
books.c: Solomon's glory and the temple's splendor fade; one greater than Solomon and the true temple is Jesus (Matt 12:42; John 2:19-21).

books.t: The long fall: exile comes at last
ls: God sends prophet after prophet in patience before judgment falls.
National ruin follows spiritual ruin — idolatry destroys from within.
Even in judgment God preserves a remnant and the lamp of David.
books.c: The preserved line of David, flickering but never extinguished, carries the promise to Bethlehem.

books.t: God's people retold: worship at the center
ls: God's covenant faithfulness runs through every generation of the genealogies.
Worship deserves our best order, skill, and joy.
Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good — His steadfast love endures forever.
books.c: The genealogy from Adam through David is the family tree that Matthew 1 completes in Jesus.

books.t: If my people humble themselves
ls: Revival begins with humbling, prayer, seeking God, and turning from sin.
The kings who sought the LORD prospered; those who forsook Him fell.
God's eyes run throughout the earth to strengthen wholehearted hearts.
books.c: The temple's filled-with-glory dedication anticipates God dwelling among us in Christ (John 1:14).

books.t: Return and rebuild: God stirs His people
ls: God moves even pagan kings' hearts to accomplish His promises.
Set your heart to study God's Word, do it, and teach it — in that order.
Restoration requires repentance, not just relocation.
books.c: The return from exile is a small resurrection — the greater return from sin's exile comes through Christ.

books.t: Rebuilding walls with sword and trowel
ls: Prayer and planning belong together; so do work and watchfulness.
The joy of the LORD is your strength.
Reform must be renewed — hearts drift even after revival.
books.c: Nehemiah's grief-driven intercession for a ruined city foreshadows Jesus weeping over Jerusalem.

books.t: Providence: the unseen God saves
ls: God's name is never mentioned — yet His hand moves in every 'coincidence.'
Courage means risking position and life for God's people: 'If I perish, I perish.'
You were placed where you are for such a time as this.
books.c: A mediator risks death, uninvited before the throne, to save the condemned — a portrait of our Advocate.

books.t: Suffering and the God who is enough
ls: The righteous do suffer — simple formulas about suffering are false comfort.
We may bring our anguish honestly to God; He is big enough for our questions.
Seeing God is better than getting answers: 'now my eye sees you.'
books.c: Job's cry for a mediator and his confession 'I know that my Redeemer lives' are answered in Jesus.

books.t: The prayer book of every heart
ls: Every emotion — praise, grief, fury, fear, joy — can be prayed.
Blessed is the one whose delight is God's Word, whose refuge is God Himself.
Praise is the destination of the whole story: let everything that has breath praise the LORD.
books.c: The Psalms are Jesus' own songbook: His suffering (Ps 22), His resurrection (Ps 16), His reign (Ps 2, 110).

books.t: Wisdom: skill in the fear of the LORD
ls: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom.
Words, money, work, friendship, desire — every ordinary thing is a spiritual thing.
Trust in the LORD with all your heart; lean not on your own understanding.
books.c: Wisdom personified, present at creation and calling in the streets, finds its fullness in Christ, the wisdom of God (1 Cor 1:24).

books.t: Vapor: life under the sun without God
ls: Pleasure, wealth, work, and wisdom cannot bear the weight of being your meaning.
Death levels everything 'under the sun' — so receive each day as God's gift.
The end of the matter: fear God and keep His commandments.
books.c: The Preacher's honest despair is the ache Jesus answers: abundant life that death cannot cancel.

books.t: Love strong as death
ls: Married love — desire, delight, faithfulness — is God's good creation.
Love is not to be awakened before its time; covenant guards the flame.
Many waters cannot quench love.
books.c: The Bridegroom's delight in his bride images Christ's love for His church (Eph 5:25-32).

books.t: The Holy One of Israel: judgment and comfort
ls: God is high and holy, and the nations are dust on His scales — yet He dwells with the contrite.
Comfort my people: sin is judged, but grace speaks tenderly and prepares a highway home.
God's servant suffers in the place of sinners — pierced for our transgressions.
books.c: Isaiah is the Gospel in the Old Testament: virgin-born Immanuel (7:14), Wonderful Counselor (9:6), the Suffering Servant (53), the anointed preacher of good news (61:1).

books.t: The weeping prophet and the new covenant
ls: God's word burns like fire — speak it whether or not anyone listens.
The heart is deceitful above all things; only God can give a new one.
Even under judgment, God plans a future and a hope for His people.
books.c: The promised new covenant — law on hearts, sins remembered no more — is sealed by Jesus' blood (Luke 22:20).

books.t: Grief that still hopes
ls: It is right to lament — to bring ruin and grief honestly before God.
His mercies are new every morning even in the ashes; great is His faithfulness.
God does not afflict from His heart; His judgments aim at restoration.
books.c: The man of sorrows who sat weeping over a destroyed city points to the Man of Sorrows who wept over it again.

books.t: The glory departs — and promises to return
ls: God's glory will not share a temple with idols — sin drives out blessing.
God will give a new heart of flesh and put His own Spirit within His people.
Dry bones live again when God's word and breath come — no one is beyond His reviving.
books.c: The good Shepherd who seeks the scattered flock Himself (34:11-16) is Jesus' self-description in John 10.

books.t: God rules the kingdoms of men
ls: Conviction may cost you the furnace or the lions' den — God is able to deliver, but even if not, we will not bow.
Pride brings kings to eat grass; heaven rules, and the humble are lifted.
History is not chaos: every empire falls, and God's kingdom stands forever.
books.c: One like a son of man receives everlasting dominion from the Ancient of Days — Jesus' favorite title for Himself.

books.t: Scandalous love for an unfaithful bride
ls: Sin is not rule-breaking only — it is adultery against a loving God.
God buys back the unfaithful at His own cost and calls them 'my people' again.
He desires steadfast love, not empty sacrifice.
books.c: Hosea buying back Gomer from the slave block is the gospel in miniature: Christ redeems His compromised bride.

books.t: The day of the LORD and the outpoured Spirit
ls: Calamity is a summons: return to the LORD with all your heart.
Rend your hearts and not your garments — He is gracious and merciful.
God promises to pour out His Spirit on all flesh.
books.c: Peter preaches Pentecost from Joel 2 — the promise poured out by the risen Jesus (Acts 2).

books.t: Let justice roll down like waters
ls: Religious performance without justice for the poor disgusts God.
Privilege increases accountability: you only have I known — therefore I will punish.
God's plumb line measures every crooked wall — and He promises to rebuild David's fallen booth.
books.c: The rebuilt booth of David that gathers the nations (9:11-12) is fulfilled in the church of Jesus (Acts 15:16-17).

books.t: Pride goes down: Edom's fall
ls: Gloating over a brother's calamity invites God's judgment.
The pride of your heart has deceived you — soaring nests are torn down.
As you have done, it shall be done to you; but Zion will be delivered.
books.c: The kingdom shall be the LORD's — the final verdict Jesus' reign makes certain.

books.t: A missionary God and a reluctant prophet
ls: You cannot outrun God's call — or His mercy.
God's compassion extends to enemies we would rather see judged.
Salvation belongs to the LORD — even the storm and the fish obey Him.
books.c: Jesus gives 'the sign of Jonah': three days in the deep, then rescue that brings mercy to the nations (Matt 12:40).

books.t: What does the LORD require?
ls: Do justice, love kindness, walk humbly with your God.
Leaders who devour the flock face the Shepherd's judgment.
Who is a God like You, pardoning iniquity, casting sins into the depths of the sea?
books.c: From little Bethlehem comes forth the ruler whose origin is from ancient days (5:2) — quoted at Jesus' birth.

books.t: The LORD avenges: Nineveh's end
ls: God's patience with evil is long but not endless.
The LORD is a stronghold in the day of trouble; He knows those who take refuge in Him.
No empire built on blood outlasts His verdict.
books.c: The feet of him who brings good news of peace (1:15) — the herald language Paul applies to gospel preachers (Rom 10:15).

books.t: Living by faith when God confuses you
ls: Take your 'how long?' and 'why?' directly to God — then wait at the watchpost.
The righteous shall live by his faith.
Though the fig tree fails and the stalls are empty, yet I will rejoice in the LORD.
books.c: 'The righteous shall live by faith' becomes the backbone of the gospel of grace (Rom 1:17; Gal 3:11).

books.t: Hidden in the day of wrath, quieted by love
ls: The day of the LORD sweeps away every proud refuge.
Seek the LORD, seek righteousness, seek humility — perhaps you may be hidden.
God rejoices over His restored people with singing.
books.c: The King of Israel in your midst (3:15) who removes judgment is Jesus among His people.

books.t: First things first: build God's house
ls: Consider your ways: paneled houses and neglected worship explain empty harvests.
Work, for I am with you — God's presence fuels obedience.
The latter glory of this house shall be greater than the former.
books.c: The greater glory came when the Lord Himself walked into that second temple.

books.t: The King is coming — humble, on a donkey
ls: Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit, says the LORD.
God removes His people's filthy garments and clothes them clean.
They will look on Him whom they pierced and mourn — and a fountain for sin will be opened.
books.c: Palm Sunday, thirty pieces of silver, the struck shepherd, the pierced one — Zechariah reads like a Passion narrative written five centuries early.

books.t: Wearied words and a coming sunrise
ls: Half-hearted offerings say what we really think of God.
God hates faithlessness in marriage and robbery in worship.
For those who fear His name, the sun of righteousness will rise with healing.
books.c: The messenger who prepares the way (3:1) is John the Baptist; the Lord who suddenly comes to His temple is Jesus. Then — four hundred years of silence, until a cry in Bethlehem.

books.t: The King and His kingdom
ls: Jesus is the promised Messiah — Matthew shows fulfillment after fulfillment.
Kingdom righteousness exceeds rule-keeping: it transforms the heart (Sermon on the Mount).
The King's final word is a commission: make disciples of all nations.
books.c: Immanuel — God with us — from the genealogy's climax to 'I am with you always.'

books.t: The Servant who came to give His life
ls: Jesus acts with immediate, breathtaking authority over disease, demons, storms, and death.
Discipleship means taking up a cross, not climbing a ladder.
The Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many.
books.c: The centurion's confession at the cross — 'Truly this man was the Son of God' — is the book's whole point.

books.t: The Savior who seeks the lost
ls: The gospel is for outsiders: shepherds, sinners, Samaritans, tax collectors, women, the poor.
Prayer and the Holy Spirit thread through Jesus' whole ministry.
The Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost.
books.c: From the manger to the empty tomb, Luke's careful history shows a Savior whose mercy reaches farther than anyone expected.

books.t: Believe and have life in His name
ls: Jesus is God the Son: the Word made flesh, the great I AM.
Eternal life is knowing the Father through the Son — beginning now.
Love one another as I have loved you: the mark of His disciples.
books.c: Seven signs and seven 'I AM' statements build one verdict: these are written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God.

books.t: The unstoppable gospel
ls: The risen Jesus builds His church by His Spirit through ordinary, praying people.
Persecution scatters believers — and spreads the gospel like wind spreads seed.
From Jerusalem to Rome, no prison, storm, or council can chain the word of God.
books.c: Acts is Jesus' continuing work: what He began to do, His body now does among all nations.

books.t: The righteousness of God, by faith
ls: All have sinned — religious and pagan alike stand guilty before God.
God justifies the ungodly freely, by grace, through faith in Jesus' blood.
Therefore: living sacrifice, transformed mind, love without hypocrisy.
books.c: The gospel is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes — Christ crucified and risen is its whole content.

books.t: The cross-shaped church
ls: The message of the cross upends worldly wisdom, status, and division.
Your body and your gatherings belong to the Lord — purity and order matter.
Love is greater than every gift; the resurrection is the hinge of everything.
books.c: Christ crucified — a stumbling block to some, but to the called, the power and wisdom of God; and Christ risen, the firstfruits of those who sleep.

books.t: Strength in weakness
ls: Ministry is treasure in jars of clay — afflicted but not crushed.
Godly grief produces repentance; generous giving flows from grace.
My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.
books.c: He who knew no sin was made sin for us, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God (5:21).

books.t: Set free: no other gospel
ls: Adding works to grace is not a variation of the gospel — it is its loss.
Justified by faith, adopted as sons, heirs of the promise to Abraham.
Walk by the Spirit: freedom is for love, and the Spirit bears His own fruit.
books.c: I have been crucified with Christ; the life I now live, I live by faith in the Son of God who loved me and gave Himself for me.

books.t: One new people, seated with Christ
ls: You were dead in sin — made alive by grace alone, through faith alone.
Christ has made Jew and Gentile one new humanity; the church is God's masterpiece.
Walk worthy: in unity, purity, Spirit-filled households, and the whole armor of God.
books.c: God's eternal plan is to unite all things in Christ — and to display His grace in the church forever.

books.t: Joy that circumstances cannot touch
ls: Partnership in the gospel turns even prison into an outpost of joy.
Have this mind among yourselves: Christ emptied Himself to the point of the cross.
Rejoice in the Lord always; the peace of God guards hearts beyond understanding.
books.c: To live is Christ, to die is gain — the whole letter breathes contentment in Him alone.

books.t: Christ is all: complete in Him
ls: Jesus is the image of the invisible God — Creator, Sustainer, Head, Firstborn from the dead.
Philosophy, ritual, and asceticism add nothing to a believer already complete in Christ.
Set your minds on things above; let Christ's word dwell richly as you live it out at home and work.
books.c: In Him the whole fullness of deity dwells bodily — and you have been filled in Him.

books.t: Hope that works while it waits
ls: The gospel arrives in power and turns people from idols to serve the living God.
Holy living — in purity, love, and honest work — pleases God.
Grieve with hope: the Lord Himself will descend, and we will always be with Him.
books.c: Waiting for God's Son from heaven, whom He raised — Jesus who delivers us from the wrath to come.

books.t: Stand firm until He comes
ls: Present suffering will be repaid with rest when Jesus is revealed.
Do not be shaken by end-times panic; lawlessness will not outlast the Lord's breath.
Idleness is not spirituality — do not grow weary in doing good.
books.c: The day of the Lord belongs to the Lord Jesus, whose coming destroys every counterfeit.

books.t: Order in God's household
ls: The saying is trustworthy: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners.
Godly leaders are proven by character before they are given charge.
Godliness with contentment is great gain; fight the good fight of the faith.
books.c: There is one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus, who gave Himself as a ransom for all.

books.t: Guard the deposit, finish the race
ls: Fan into flame the gift of God; He gave us a spirit not of fear but of power, love, and self-control.
Entrust the gospel to faithful people who will teach others also — four generations in one verse (2:2).
All Scripture is breathed out by God and equips for every good work.
books.c: Remember Jesus Christ, risen from the dead — Paul's dying charge and the church's living hope.

books.t: Grace that trains us for good works
ls: Sound doctrine and sound living are inseparable.
Appoint elders of proven character to set the church in order.
We are saved not by works of righteousness but by the washing of regeneration.
books.c: We wait for our blessed hope: the appearing of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ.

books.t: Receive him as you would receive me
ls: The gospel turns a runaway slave into a beloved brother.
Christian appeal works by love, not compulsion.
'Charge it to my account' — imputation in one sentence.
books.c: Paul's offer to pay Onesimus's debt mirrors Christ, who charged our debt to Himself.

books.t: Jesus is better: don't drift
ls: Jesus is superior to angels, Moses, and every priest — the exact imprint of God's nature.
His one sacrifice does what a thousand altars never could: it perfects forever.
Therefore hold fast, draw near with confidence, and run the race looking to Jesus.
books.c: A great High Priest who sympathizes with our weakness, a new covenant in His blood, an unshakable kingdom.

books.t: Faith that works
ls: Count trials as joy — tested faith produces steadfastness.
Be doers of the word; religion that ignores the needy and unbridles the tongue is worthless.
Faith without works is dead; humble yourselves and He will exalt you.
books.c: The wisdom from above and the royal law of love both come from the Lord of glory, Jesus.

books.t: Exiles: hope under fire
ls: A living hope through the resurrection guards you through grief and trial.
You are a chosen race, a royal priesthood — so live honorably among unbelievers.
Suffering for good is grace; entrust your soul to a faithful Creator.
books.c: He Himself bore our sins in His body on the tree — by His wounds you have been healed.

books.t: Growing in grace while scoffers scoff
ls: His divine power has granted everything needed for life and godliness — so add virtue to faith.
False teachers promise freedom and deliver slavery.
The Lord is not slow but patient, not wishing that any should perish.
books.c: We did not follow myths: eyewitnesses of His majesty await the day the Morning Star rises.

books.t: God is light, God is love: assurance
ls: Walking in the light means confessing sin, not pretending sinlessness.
Love one another — anyone who hates a brother walks in darkness.
These things are written that you may KNOW you have eternal life.
books.c: The blood of Jesus cleanses from all sin; He is the propitiation, our Advocate with the Father.

books.t: Truth and love walk together
ls: Walking in truth is the parent's deepest joy.
Love is defined by obedience, not sentiment.
Do not receive teaching that denies Christ come in the flesh.
books.c: Abiding in the teaching of Christ is having both the Father and the Son.

books.t: Support the workers of the truth
ls: No greater joy than to hear that my children walk in the truth.
Hospitality to gospel workers makes you a fellow worker for the truth.
Imitate good, not evil — Diotrephes' love of preeminence is the anti-pattern.
books.c: Workers go out 'for the sake of the Name' — the Name above every name.

books.t: Contend for the faith once delivered
ls: False teaching creeps in quietly and turns grace into license.
Build yourselves up in faith, pray in the Spirit, keep yourselves in God's love, show mercy to doubters.
God is able to keep you from stumbling and present you blameless with great joy.
books.c: Kept for Jesus Christ — and kept BY Him, the only God our Savior, be glory forever.

books.t: The Lamb wins: behold, I am coming soon
ls: Jesus walks among His churches now — He sees, commends, corrects, and promises.
History's storms rage under a throne that never shakes; the Lamb who was slain is worthy to open the scroll.
Every tear wiped away, death no more, the dwelling of God with man — and the gates never shut.
books.c: The Lion is the Lamb: Alpha and Omega, the bright Morning Star. The Bible's last prayer is the church's oldest one — 'Come, Lord Jesus.'
